name: Artificial Neural Net - Multilayer
catalogPath: Sample Models/Computer Science/Artificial Neural Net - Multilayer
miniText: How does adding nonlinear hidden units change what a small network can learn? NetLogo Artificial Neural Net Multilayer propagates weighted inputs through a hidden layer and sigmoid activations, then adjusts weights using supervised errors. Rosenblatt [1] supplies the single-perceptron reference point, Rumelhart and colleagues [2] establish backpropagation learning, and Cybenko [3] provides a theoretical account of approximation by sigmoidal networks. The teaching example makes the architectural contrast with exclusive OR visible: hidden representations can separate cases that one linear threshold cannot. Random initial weights, learning rate, hidden structure, and the finite training sequence affect progress. Expressive capacity is distinct from successful optimization, and decreasing training error alone does not establish generalization. The baseline illustrates a deliberately small learning mechanism rather than modern large-scale neural training or a physiological model of a brain.
